paper.title_en: Practical Biometric-Authenticated Quantum Key Agreement via A Single Quantum Channel
paper.abstract_en: When designing a practical biometric-authenticated two-party quantum key agreement (QKA) protocol, it is essential to comprehensively consider factors such as authentication mechanisms, allocation of quantum resources, reliability of quantum channels, and qubit efficiency. This paper introduces a fully trusted registry that leverages fuzzy extractors for participant registration and authentication, uses Bell states as the primary quantum resource, and integrates entanglement swapping of Bell states with Bell measurements and classical binary encoding to achieve feasible qubit efficiency in generating the final shared key by a single quantum channel. Additionally, the proposed protocol has been successfully simulated using Qiskit, and its correctness has been rigorously verified. Further security analysis and performance comparisons show this protocol can achieve optimal results within the constraints of current quantum technologies.
